question: Do the bond distances of a not-all-equal base, read from its allowed states, determine those states? Unsigned and signed pairwise tables, bond sets (plain, signed ties, with missing states) and prime implicates (control), all relations at n = 4, 5, 6 and 400,000 random knot sets at n = 7.

definitions.bond: a set of >= 2 distinctions whose projection is constrained and free after forgetting any one member
definitions.bond distance: size of the smallest bond holding the pair, minus one

forbidden_inputs: Changing readings, predictions or decision rules after seeing registered results
cheapest_meaningful_control: Prime implicates, which determine the relation by theorem (G).

predictions.D1: (a) collides at n = 4: 12 tables for 16 relations
predictions.D2: (b) same at n = 4, first finer than (a) at n = 5
predictions.D3: (c) clean at n = 4, collides at n = 5 (isomorphic)
predictions.D4: (c-s) clean at n = 5, collides at n = 6 or 7

decision_rules.each prediction: holds or fails as stated in the pre-registration

stop_rule: One run; A97 status; referee hand-off; report.
runtime: Under ten minutes on four processes.
